verdict_reason: Mapping and role tests are sound, but two titles give the mapper credit for rules the request and response constructors own, and one ISO-8601 test repeats another test's assertions.

todos.issue: Two titles credit AddressMapper with rules it does not own. toEntity_keepsTheFirstOfEachRepeatedRole (:189) passes only because AddressRequest's compact constructor runs roles.stream().distinct() before toEntity is called, and that rule is already tested at AddressRequestValidationTest.roles_collapseRepeatsToTheFirstOfEach (:261). toResponse_failsLoudWhenARequiredFieldIsNull (:84) proves AddressResponse's Objects.requireNonNull guard, already tested per field by AddressResponseTest.compactConstructor_rejectsNullOnGuardedFields (:51). A reader trusts the titles and believes the mapper dedupes and null-checks.
todos.fix: Must: each rule is tested once, in the test class of the type that owns it, and no AddressMapperTest title claims behaviour the mapper does not perform. One way: delete both tests from AddressMapperTest, since AddressRequestValidationTest and AddressResponseTest already cover the rules.

todos.issue: response_serialisesInstantFieldsAsIso8601NotEpochMillis (:129) cannot fail on its own. Its only assertions are isTextual() on createdAt and modifiedAt, and the test above it (:95) already asserts json.get("createdAt").asText() equals "2026-07-01T09:00:00Z" and the same for modifiedAt. Epoch millis would turn both red, so this test adds no proof. Its predecessor also asserted WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS was disabled; that line is gone and nothing replaced it.
todos.fix: Must: every test in the file fails for a reason no other test in the file already catches. One way: delete response_serialisesInstantFieldsAsIso8601NotEpochMillis, because the camelCase test's exact ISO-8601 string assertions already prove it.
